newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian customs urges higher food import duties.
newsitem.headline: Russian customs urges higher food import duties.

text.p: The head of Russia's State Customs Committee said on Wednesday Russia should raise import duties for foodstuffs and lower those for cars.
Anatoly Kruglov told a news conference the state should in the first place protect domestic producers of basic foodstuffs such as meat, eggs, milk and dairy products.
"The state should aim at maximum protection of our own foodstuffs producers. This is an element of the economic security of the state," Kruglov said.

Many Russian officials have stepped up protectionist talk in the past year because of concern about domestic production. Many propose higher import duties on alcohol and flour and sugar, as well as quotas for many items.
Others say Russia cannot feed itself without imports, while protectionist measures could dent Russia's relationship with the World Trade Organisation, which Russia wants to join.
According to trade sources, imports account for up to 45 percent of the domestic food market.
Kruglov said that protectionist measures did not always give the desired effect, which was the case with Russia's automobile industry.
Kruglov said his committee wanted car import duties to be lowered.

"We have in fact prohibitive duties on car imports, but this has not led to a rise in Russian car-making," Kruglov said. "This measure resulted in only one thing -- smuggling of foreign cars into Russia."
